macros.name: addtoOptAttachments
macros.doc: The \addtoOptAttachments command is a way of optionally attaching a file without the input.

macros.name: afterRequirementPassedJS
macros.doc: A hook into the end of the \requiresVersion command for additional JS to be executed.

macros.name: ahyperlink
macros.doc: The default behavior of \ahyperref (and \ahyperlink) is to set up a link from parent to child. \ahyperlink and \ahyperref are identical in all respects except for how it interprets the destination.

macros.name: ahyperref
macros.doc: \ahyperref is used to jump to a destination (as specified by the dest key, listed in Table 2, page 46) defined by the \label command, whereas \ahyperlink is used to jump to a destination (as specified by the dest key) defined by the \hypertarget of hyperref.

macros.name: animeBld
macros.doc: The command \animeBld increments ocSeq, and names the layer so that the JS can run through the layers in an orderly way.

macros.name: animeSetup
macros.doc: The argument is the key-value pairs of \btnAnime or of the ocgAnime environment. The command processes the key-value pairs.

macros.name: autolabelNum
macros.doc: For PDFs (or other files) embedded using the attachments option, use the \autolabelNum command.

macros.name: btnAnime
macros.doc: Create a series of stacked buttons that hold and display the frames of the animation; it also creates the control buttons.

macros.name: btnanimebtnsep
macros.doc: The space between control buttons is determined by \btnanimebtnsep, the default definition is \newcommand{\btnanimebtnsep}{1bp}.

macros.name: btnAnimePresets
macros.doc: You can influence of the appearance of buttons that display the images by using the command \btnAnimePresets.

macros.name: btnanimerowsep
macros.doc: The vertical space between two rows of buttons is \btnanimerowsep, the default definition is \newcommand{\btnanimerowsep}{1bp}.

macros.name: certifyInvisibleSign
macros.doc: This command uses the trusted version of certifyInvisibleSign to sign.

macros.name: DeclareAnime
macros.doc: This sets the basic parameters of an anime: the base name for the animation, the speed of the animation as measured in milliseconds, and the number of frames to appear in the anime.

macros.name: DeclareInitView
macros.doc: The \DeclareInitView command is a “data structure” for setting the Initial View of the Document Properties dialog box, see Figure 1.

macros.name: declareMultiImages
macros.doc: The command \declareMultiImages loops through the list, calling \declareImageAndPlacement with the current set of KV-pairs.

macros.name: embedMultiPageImages
macros.doc: The command embeds (in the document) and optionally places a series of icons all of which are pages of the same PDF file.

macros.name: executeSave
macros.doc: This command saves the current file so you don’t have do it yourself.

macros.name: extractPages
macros.doc: API to extract pages from a newly formed document.

macros.name: importDataObject
macros.doc: Attaches a file to the PDF.

macros.name: insertCtrlButtons
macros.doc: This command can be used to place the anime controls somewhere other than at the default location (under the anime).

macros.name: insertPages
macros.doc: Inserts pages into the PDF, useful for inserting pages of difference sizes, such as tables or figures, into a LaTeX document which requires that all page be of a fixed size.

macros.name: insertPreDocAssembly
macros.doc: This command is to be used within the docassembly environment, and expands to all the JavaScript lines created by \declareImageAndPlacement.

macros.name: mailDoc
macros.doc: Used by eEnvelope to programmatically mail a document.

macros.name: makePDFPackage
macros.doc: To create a PDF Package, embed all files in the parent and use the command \makePDFPackage in the preamble to package the attachments.

macros.name: placeAnimeCtrlBtnFaces
macros.doc: This command associate the icon set to be used for the button appearances of the buttons used to control the button animation.

macros.name: placeImage
macros.doc: Creates a readonly push button with an icon only appearance.

macros.name: requiredVersionMsg
macros.doc: When the document is opened outside a web browser and the version number requirement is not met, the message contained in \requiredVersionMsg appears in an alert box.

macros.name: requiredVersionMsgRedirect
macros.doc: When the document is opened in a browser and the version number requirement is not met the message contained in \requiredVersionMsgRedirect appears in an alert box.

macros.name: requiresVersion
macros.doc: For \requiresVersion, the parameter version_number is the minimal version number that this document is made for. If the version number of the viewer is less than version_number, an alert box appears, and the document is silently closed, if outside a browser, or redirected, if inside a browser.

macros.name: resetahyperDefaults
macros.doc: Use \resetahyperDefaults to cancel out the user defined defaults.

macros.name: setDefaultFS
macros.doc: Set the default fullscreen behavior of Adobe Reader/Acrobat by using \setDefaultFS in the preamble.

macros.name: sigInfo
macros.doc: The \sigInfo command is used for entering signing formation into what will become an object.

macros.name: signatureSetSeedValue
macros.doc: The Acrobat JavaScript methods Field.signatureSetSeedValue is implemented through the LaTeX comment \signatureSetSeedValue.

macros.name: signatureSign
macros.doc: The function \signatureSign takes the info in the oSigInfo object, gets the security handler object, logs into the handler, calls signatureSetSeedValue if the sv property is in the oSigInfo object, and signs the field.

macros.name: texHelp
macros.doc: The \texHelp is a command for creating a rollover for some text. When the user rolls over the text, a defined layer is made visible with helpful information.

macros.name: texPrintHelp
macros.doc: The \texPrintHelp command reduces to \texHelp or typesets its second argument.

macros.name: xBld
macros.doc: The basic command for creating a layer is \xBld. The content of the layer is set off by the \xBld/\eBld pair.

envs.name: ocgAnime
envs.doc: OCG animation is available through the ocgAnime environment.
